discoveries.headline: Crypto: the basics, from the UK's financial regulator
discoveries.why: The FCA's plain guide to what crypto is and what can go wrong. Its own example: Bitcoin peaked at £93,947 on 6 October 2025 and was down 30.44% by 1 December. Read it before you buy anything, and only put in what you could afford to lose. Education, not advice.

discoveries.headline: How much CO2 can the world still emit?
discoveries.why: While COP31 talks go on in Antalya, Hannah Ritchie and Pablo Rosado put the stakes in one chart: the 1.5°C carbon budget equals only about 3.5 years of current emissions, and at today's rate it runs out around 2030. One minute of reading that makes every headline from the summit clearer.
discoveries.meta_credit: Our World in Data · Hannah Ritchie and Pablo Rosado

discoveries.headline: A toad swims across its woodland pond
discoveries.why: Paul Hobson took top honours at the 2026 British Wildlife Photography Awards with a black-and-white toad gliding through a pond near Sheffield. Fifteen images of the wild things living right next door. Look closer at your own patch this weekend.
discoveries.meta_credit: Popular Science · British Wildlife Photography Awards
discoveries.credit: © Paul Hobson, British Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026

discoveries.headline: Jack Kornfield: grounding, gratitude and presence
discoveries.why: A guided sit recorded at Spirit Rock's Monday night class: gratitude for breath, body, heart and mind, then opening to the wide field of awareness beyond thoughts. Kornfield has taught meditation since 1974, and it shows in how gently he leads. Perfect for a slow Saturday morning.
discoveries.source: Heart Wisdom with Jack Kornfield · Be Here Now Network
discoveries.meta_credit: Be Here Now Network · Jack Kornfield

discoveries.headline: Why are we curious about some things and not others?
discoveries.why: Cognitive scientist Tommy Blanchard explains why curiosity peaks when we know a little, not nothing and not everything, and why most of us understand bicycles and toilets far less than we think. A friendly nudge to learn just enough about something new to get hooked.

discoveries.headline: A Piece of Red Cloth wins the Prime Minister's fiction prize
discoveries.why: This year's Prime Minister's Literary Award for fiction went to a book made together by Leonie Norrington, Merrkiyawuy Ganambarr-Stubbs, Djawa Burarrwanga and Djawundil Maymuru. Each category winner receives $80,000. Champion it: borrow it, buy it, or tell one friend.
discoveries.meta_credit: Creative Australia · Prime Minister's Literary Awards

discoveries.headline: Getting ready for pitta season
discoveries.why: Summer is on its way in Sydney, and Ayurveda calls it pitta season: hot, sharp and fiery. Erin Casperson of the Kripalu School of Ayurveda shares simple cooling rituals, from cool (not iced) water with lime and mint to swapping sesame oil for coconut oil in self-massage. General information, not medical advice.

discoveries.headline: Ten-minute morning yoga for beginners
discoveries.why: Kassandra's short, prop-free flow for anyone, with one kind twist: instead of savasana it ends with a one-minute seated meditation, so you won't drift back to sleep. Bend your knees generously in Downward Dog; mornings are for being gentle.

discoveries.headline: Four minutes a day, real gains
discoveries.why: In a Penn State study of 97 people with an average age of 74, four moves done for 30 seconds each (push-ups, chair stands, rows and stair steps) improved strength and balance. People stuck with it on 81% of days. Proof that a tiny daily ritual counts.
discoveries.meta_credit: News-Medical · Penn State College of Medicine
